author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.57.2. Comments verified against the body; they still describe it. The rot flag fired because the class gained state, not because anything it says stopped being true.

What changed: Handler now carries filter_prefix and force alongside repo, bound by serve() onto the generated subclass. Both the page route and /api/map read them, and that pairing is load-bearing - the live refresh must render the SAME view the page was built from, or a note written in a filtered console would refresh into the unfiltered map and the graph would change shape under the reader's cursor mid-write.

The reason the flags exist at all: _map_payload used to call export(force=True) unconditionally, silently overriding viz's readability guard at VIZ_WARN_ENTITIES (1500). The CLI refuses above it and tells you to filter; the console rendered prometheus's 12,987 entities without a word. The guard's own message ends "Nothing is ever sampled silently", and this was the single caller that did. serve() now evaluates the payload BEFORE binding a port and raises, so the console cannot come up serving a view the CLI would have refused.
